name: Bali
summary: Resort beaches in Nusa Dua, cliff temples in Uluwatu, Nusa Penida's coastline, Ubud's rice terraces and volcano sunrises, then Canggu sunsets.

places.name: Marriott's Bali Nusa Dua Gardens
places.blurb: Resort hotel in Bali's gated Nusa Dua enclave, a short shuttle from the beach. Bookable with Marriott points, which is why points travellers start their trip here.

places.name: Nusa Dua Beach / Geger Beach / Pandawa Beach
places.blurb: Three calm, white-sand beaches on the sheltered east side of the Bukit. Pandawa sits below carved limestone cliffs; Geger is the quiet local favourite.

places.name: Bali Collection
places.blurb: Open-air shopping and dining complex inside the Nusa Dua resort enclave. Handy for essentials and a stroll rather than a destination in itself.

places.name: Uluwatu Temple
places.blurb: Thousand-year-old sea temple perched on a 70 m cliff edge at Bali's southwestern tip. One of the island's six holiest temples, famous for sunsets and bold macaques.

places.name: Kecak Dance Performance
places.blurb: Traditional fire dance performed at sunset in Uluwatu Temple's clifftop amphitheatre, with a chanting choir of dozens of men instead of instruments. Telling of the Ramayana epic.

places.name: Bumbu Bali
places.blurb: Long-running Balinese fine-dining restaurant by chef Heinz von Holzen, known for its rijsttafel set menu and cooking school. A classic for authentic Balinese food.

places.name: Ferry from Sanur to Nusa Penida
places.blurb: Fast boats cross from Sanur to Nusa Penida in about 45 minutes. Book a morning boat; the strait gets choppy in the afternoon.

places.name: West Nusa Penida (Kelingking Beach, Angel's Billabong, Broken Beach, Crystal Bay)
places.blurb: Day-tour circuit of Nusa Penida's west coast: the T-rex-shaped Kelingking cliff, Angel's Billabong rock pool, Broken Beach's natural arch and Crystal Bay for snorkelling.

places.name: Diamond Beach
places.blurb: White-sand cove on Nusa Penida's east coast, reached by a cliff-carved staircase, with palm trees and diamond-shaped rock pinnacles in the surf.

places.name: Maruti Beach Club
places.blurb: Laid-back beach club on Nusa Penida where a sunbed comes with a minimum food-and-drink spend. A rest stop between the island's viewpoints.

places.name: Sanur to Ubud Drive
places.blurb: Private car from the coast up to Ubud, about 90 minutes depending on traffic. Drivers usually stop at sights on request.

places.name: Ubud Art Market
places.blurb: Traditional market opposite Ubud's royal palace selling woven bags, sarongs, carvings and art. Free to wander; bargaining is expected.

places.name: Mount Batur Sunrise Hike
places.blurb: Pre-dawn hike up a 1,717 m active volcano for sunrise above a sea of clouds and the caldera lake. About two hours up on a well-trodden path with a guide.

places.name: Tegalalang Rice Terraces
places.blurb: Bali's most photographed rice terraces, carved into a river valley north of Ubud using the island's thousand-year-old subak irrigation system.

places.name: Goa Gajah & Pura Gunung Lebah
places.blurb: Goa Gajah, the 9th-century 'Elephant Cave' sanctuary with its carved demon-mouth entrance, paired with the small river-junction temple Pura Gunung Lebah in Ubud.

places.name: Copper Kitchen and Bar
places.blurb: Rooftop restaurant at Bisma Eight in Ubud doing modern plates with local produce. A dressier dinner option without resort prices.

places.name: Alchemy / Umah Pizza / Warung Di Koi
places.blurb: A trio of easy Ubud eats: Alchemy's famous raw-vegan breakfast bar, wood-fired pizza at Umah, and cheap local plates at Warung Di Koi.

places.name: No Mas Bar / CP Lounge
places.blurb: Ubud's low-key nightlife pair: cocktails at No Más and late-night drinks and live music at CP Lounge.

places.name: Ubud Yoga (Radiantly Alive / Ubud Yoga House)
places.blurb: Drop-in classes at Ubud's best-known studios, Radiantly Alive and Ubud Yoga House, from beginner flows to aerial. Part of why Ubud became Bali's wellness capital.

places.name: Pura Tanah Lot
places.blurb: 16th-century temple on a rock just offshore, cut off at high tide. One of Bali's most sacred sea temples and its most famous sunset silhouette.

places.name: Canggu Beach Clubs (The Lawn, Finns, La Brisa)
places.blurb: Canggu's beachfront clubs: grassy sunset drinks at The Lawn, pool parties at Finns, and driftwood-chic La Brisa. Entry is free; daybeds carry a minimum spend.

places.name: The Shady Shack
places.blurb: Breezy vegetarian cafe by Canggu's rice fields that became one of Bali's best-known healthy-food spots. Expect smoothie bowls and big veggie burgers.

places.name: Coffee Cartel
places.blurb: Instagram-famous Seminyak brunch cafe known for latte art, pastel interiors and health-leaning breakfast plates.

places.name: Prana Spa
places.blurb: Moroccan-Rajasthani styled spa in Seminyak, one of Bali's most elaborate day spas, doing massages, rituals and hammam treatments.

places.name: W Hotel
places.blurb: Flashy beachfront resort on Seminyak's sand, known for its pool scene and Woobar sunsets. The splurge stay of this route.

places.name: Merah Putih
places.blurb: Striking high-ceilinged restaurant serving modern Indonesian food; the 10-dish tasting menu tours the archipelago's cuisines.

places.name: The Edge
places.blurb: Clifftop resort above Uluwatu whose day pass buys access to the famous glass-edged 'oneeighty' pool hanging over the ocean, with food-and-drink credit included.

places.name: Green Bowl Beach
places.blurb: Secluded white-sand beach at the bottom of about 300 steps on the Bukit's south coast, shared with surfers and bats in its cliff caves.

places.name: Sundays Beach Club
places.blurb: Beach club on a private white-sand cove below the cliffs at Ungasan, reached by inclinator. Day pass includes food-and-drink credit, kayaks and snorkelling.

places.name: Sarong
places.blurb: Elegant Seminyak dining room by chef Will Meyrick doing refined South-East Asian street food. A long-standing special-occasion pick.

places.name: Ubud Shopping
places.blurb: Boutique-hopping along Ubud's Jalan Dewi Sita and Hanoman streets: homeware, jewellery and clothes beyond the market stalls.

places.name: Royal Ubud Palace Fire Show
places.blurb: Evening Legong and fire dance performances in the courtyard of Puri Saren Agung, Ubud's royal palace, still home to the town's royal family.

places.name: Tirta Gangga Water Palace
places.blurb: Former royal water palace in East Bali from 1946, with koi-filled pools, fountains and stepping stones, built around a spring the Balinese hold sacred.

places.name: Gates of Heaven (Lempuyang Temple)
places.blurb: Lempuyang Temple's famous split gate framing Mount Agung. The 'reflection' in photos is a trick done with a mirror under a phone, and queues run for hours.

places.name: Ubud Rafting
places.blurb: White-water rafting on the Ayung River's class II-III rapids through jungle gorges and past waterfalls, with hotel pickup included on most tours.

places.name: Tegenungan Waterfall
places.blurb: Powerful 15 m waterfall near Ubud, one of Bali's most visited, with a swimmable pool and a staircase of viewpoints.

places.name: Tirta Empul Temple
places.blurb: Thousand-year-old water temple where Balinese Hindus queue through 13 fountain spouts for the melukat purification ritual. Visitors can join with a guide and a sarong.

itineraries.title: One week in Bali
itineraries.summary: Start slow at a Nusa Dua resort, day-trip to Nusa Penida, base in Ubud for temples and a Mount Batur sunrise hike, finish with Tanah Lot and Canggu beach clubs.
itineraries.creator: racheloffduty

items.name: SafetyWing Travel Insurance
items.note: Essential for emergency medical coverage, trip protection, and optional adventure sports coverage in Bali.
items.priceNote: Essential plan, ages 18-39, $62.72 per 4 weeks (creator: a couple bucks a day)

items.name: Marriott's Bali Nusa Dua Gardens
items.note: Great for a relaxing first day to beat jet-lag with a resort feel and dedicated beach shuttles.
items.priceNote: per night, 1-bedroom (date-dependent) (creator: bookable with Marriott points)

items.name: Nusa Dua Beach / Geger Beach / Pandawa Beach
items.note: Guaranteed beach time with reserved hotel cabanas or space on the sand for non-guests.
items.priceNote: Pandawa entry; Nusa Dua free, Geger ~IDR 5k

items.name: Bali Collection
items.note: The main spot in the area for grabbing some shopping.

items.name: Uluwatu Temple
items.note: Built on the edge of a cliff, it provides an amazing vantage point of South Bali's epic cliffs and pristine beaches.

items.name: Kecak Dance Performance
items.note: A rhythmic musical and choreographed skit performance at sunset; well worth seeing for first-timers.

items.name: Bumbu Bali
items.note: A sizable restaurant serving exclusively Balinese cuisine.
items.priceNote: rijsttafel set menu, price on site

items.name: Ferry from Sanur to Nusa Penida
items.note: A 40-minute ferry ride; wear clothes above the knees as you have to wade shin-deep in water to board.

items.name: West Nusa Penida (Kelingking Beach, Angel's Billabong, Broken Beach, Crystal Bay)
items.note: Stunning, unbelievable beaches that make the trek to the island completely worth it.
items.priceNote: shared day tour incl. boat & lunch

items.name: Diamond Beach
items.note: An epic must-visit beach on the eastern side of the island.

items.name: Maruti Beach Club
items.note: Convenient spot near the dock to relax by the pool; the smoothies are great though the food is average.
items.priceNote: sunbed minimum spend (creator: free to use facilities with food/drink purchase)

items.name: Sanur to Ubud Drive
items.note: Takes 1-2 hours depending on traffic; highly recommend arranging a private driver ahead of time.

items.name: Ubud Art Market
items.note: Wander around and pick up beautiful woven bags, scarves, or jewelry.

items.name: Mount Batur Sunrise Hike
items.note: Requires a 2 AM wake-up call, but the 1.5-2 hour guided hike yields incredible sunrise views from the volcano.

items.name: Tegalalang Rice Terraces
items.note: Make this your first stop to beat the crowds and enjoy the beautiful morning light.

items.name: Goa Gajah & Pura Gunung Lebah
items.note: Beautiful nearby temples; Goa Gajah has a carved demon entrance, and Gunung Lebah is the birthplace of Ubud.

items.name: Copper Kitchen and Bar
items.note: A fun rooftop spot perfect for a fancier night out.

items.name: Alchemy / Umah Pizza / Warung Di Koi
items.note: Great diverse eats: Alchemy for raw/vegan, Umah for cozy pizza, and Warung Di Koi for solid mie goreng.

items.name: No Mas Bar / CP Lounge
items.note: Vibrant nightlife spots for grabbing drinks, dancing to live music, and mingling.

items.name: Ubud Yoga (Radiantly Alive / Ubud Yoga House)
items.note: Take a class in open-air studios with natural lighting and views of rice terraces.

items.name: Pura Tanah Lot
items.note: Very crowded but an absolutely iconic and breathtaking spot to catch the sunset.

items.name: Canggu Beach Clubs (The Lawn, Finns, La Brisa)
items.note: Choose your vibe from open-air casual, lively poolside DJs, or reclaimed wood Mediterranean atmospheres.
items.priceNote: free entry; daybeds have min spend

items.name: The Shady Shack
items.note: A breezy, vegetarian health food cafe overlooking the rice fields.

itineraries.title: 10 days of luxury Bali
itineraries.summary: Seminyak spas and fine dining, Uluwatu cliff pools and beach clubs, Ubud culture and rice terraces, East Bali water palaces, and a Nusa Penida day trip.
itineraries.creator: vamosbitchachos

items.name: Coffee Cartel
items.note: A little coffee shop with the freshest produce and the tastiest breakfast options.

items.name: Prana Spa
items.note: A perfect place to kick back, relax, and enjoy a spa treatment.

items.name: W Hotel
items.note: Great beachfront spot with endless pools and an energetic atmosphere.

items.name: Merah Putih
items.note: Authentic Balinese fine dining with 10/10 lobster dumplings; book in advance.
items.priceNote: 10-dish tasting menu per person (creator: relatively pricey)

items.name: The Edge
items.note: Ultimate #poolgoals; make sure to reserve a table early to secure your spot.
items.priceNote: day pass incl. IDR 600k F&B credit

items.name: Green Bowl Beach
items.note: A gorgeous, secluded beach perfect for exploring.

items.name: Sundays Beach Club
items.note: An amazing beach club setting with great vibes.
items.priceNote: day pass incl. F&B credit & cable car

items.name: Sarong
items.note: Another fantastic dinner option known for excellent service and tasting menus.

items.name: Ubud Shopping
items.note: Pick up souvenirs like the popular twine bags and local household products.

items.name: Royal Ubud Palace Fire Show
items.note: A cultural evening show starting around 8:30 PM; arrive early for good seats.

items.name: Tegallalang Rice Terrace
items.note: Incredibly famous, vast rice terraces with spectacular, dream-like views.

items.name: Tirta Gangga Water Palace
items.note: Former royal home featuring beautiful carved statues, lush gardens, and iconic koi fish ponds.

items.name: Gates of Heaven (Lempuyang Temple)
items.note: Felt like a social media trap with nothing to see but two gates; not worth the hype.

items.name: Kelingking Beach
items.note: Breathtaking T-Rex shaped viewpoint; arrive early so you have energy to hike down and back up.

items.name: Crystal Bay Beach
items.note: Crystal clear water making it ideal for snorkeling, diving, or just kicking back for a tan.

items.name: Ubud Rafting
items.note: Highly rated by others as a trip highlight, though the creator skipped it due to personal preference.

items.name: Tegenungan Waterfall
items.note: A stunning, accessible waterfall located in the southern part of Bali.

items.name: Tirta Empul Temple
items.note: The creator's biggest regret to miss; watch thousands bathe in thousand-year-old curative holy springs.
